falsifiers_shipped_with_it: a PLANTED per-day artifact whose D(E0) disagrees with its own gross delta must make the recompute REFUSE
an artifact that AGREES must NOT refuse -- the other direction, so the check is not simply strict
a SHORT draw array must refuse
a digest MISMATCH between the two copies must refuse
a recompute that has never been shown to refuse is not evidence (rule 15)
filed_under: R-548(F) design round: 'DA declares the independent recompute and the era-status audit of the 08-24 hour'. The era audit is da_era_status_0824_hour.py and is already run; this is the other half.

entries.what: the single-day precedent verified at Q-DA-258
DE's ledger (READ to learn the convention, never imported for the arithmetic)

entries.at_run_time: pinned at read time and recorded in my receipt

paths_and_digests_pinned_now.note: a digest that has moved by run time is a FINDING, not a nuisance: I report the change and recompute against the new one rather than silently following it
paths_and_digests_pinned_now.read_at_both_copies: the multi-day artifact is read in the MAIN TREE and in my worktree and I refuse if they differ -- the check that would catch a mid-flight rewrite

refusal_conditions: the identity fails: D(E0) != gross_delta on any arm-day, to 1e-9
the draw array is ABSENT or SHORT of the declared per-day minimum (R-548(F): >=500 draws per arm per day). A p recomputed from fewer draws than declared is not the declared statistic
the two copies disagree -- main tree vs worktree digest of the artifact

the seed does not PIN THE DATA. R-548(F) requires the seed to pin the data by digest; a seed with no input digest means the draws are not reproducible, and I say so rather than recompute against whatever is on disk
day-set mismatch: the days in the artifact differ from the days declared, or any day is not independently verifiable as accrued by my own da_forward_day_verify re-run
fe is RECONSTRUCTED rather than READ anywhere I depend on it -- the B-4 defect, now a standing check on my own side too
status: DECLARED BEFORE ANY RUN. Nothing in this file has been computed.
what_I_will_NOT_read: BE's PICKLE (de_section81_cache_*.pkl or any successor). The recompute reads the EMITTED RECEIPT, not the producer's intermediate state: reading the pickle would make my number a second evaluation of BE's own in-memory objects rather than an independent reading of what was published, and the published artifact is what every downstream claim cites

any DE or BE module IMPORTED for the arithmetic (R-235: separate implementations are the point). I read their source to learn the convention -- as in round 55, where reading located p = level and the factor of five -- then write the arithmetic myself
DE's reported p, D, or rank AS INPUTS. Those are the things being checked

a_per_day_D_E0.definition: the decision delta at the zero-maker-fee endpoint, arm minus baseline, per day
a_per_day_D_E0.method: read each arm's and the baseline's gross_after_queue_reset_before_fees_cents from DE's emitted receipt and difference them in my own code
a_per_day_D_E0.the_check: at E0 the maker fee is zero, so D(E0) MUST equal the gross delta exactly. That identity is the check, not an assumption

b_per_day_null_location.definition: the treated arm's rank among its own per-day draws and the resulting one-sided p
b_per_day_null_location.formula: p = (1 + #{draws >= treated}) / (n + 1), one-sided, ties counting TOWARD the control
b_per_day_null_location.method: recomputed from the per-draw ARRAY, never from DE's reported p

what_this_will_NOT_establish: NOT a validation: G-counting and the R-529(A) directional ruling are untouched. Agreement between DE and me is agreement about ARITHMETIC

NOT independence of the null's DESIGN: I recompute the treated arm's location within the draws DE GENERATED. If the draw-generating design is wrong, my recompute agrees with DE and both are wrong. That is a limit of this check and it is the reviewer's to attack, not mine to close
NOT admissibility: whether the days may be used is a policy question (rule 14). I report the arithmetic and the accrual
